source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Excess dietary protein intake alone, rather than the far more complex physiologic mechanisms that are actually driving this particular kind of fluid buildup","B":"A simple, isolated increase in the client's overall fluid intake alone, rather than the more complex mechanisms actually at play in this specific condition","C":"A condition generally considered unrelated to how well the client's liver happens to be functioning at the present point in time","D":"A complex interplay of portal hypertension, decreased albumin production (leading to reduced oncotic pressure), and fluid retention mechanisms including secondary hyperaldosteronism"}}
source_row.rationale: Cirrhotic ascites results from a complex interplay of portal hypertension, decreased albumin production (leading to reduced oncotic pressure that normally keeps fluid within blood vessels), and fluid retention mechanisms including secondary hyperaldosteronism, reflecting the multifaceted pathophysiology of advanced liver disease.
